releases.title: Emplifi Reveals 87% of Marketers Agree AI Has Improved Productivity, but Fewer Than Half Can Confidently Prove Social Media ROI
releases.body:
The State of Social Media Marketing 2027 report from Emplifi, based on a survey of 405 marketers, finds AI is expanding team capacity while governance, measurement, and burnout remain open challenges.

NEW YORK, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Emplifi, a leading Autonomous CX platform, today released "The State of Social Media Marketing 2027," a report based on a survey of 405 marketing managers, directors, and executives across the US, UK, Australia, and New Zealand.

The report explores top-of-mind issues for today's marketers, including AI implementations, cross-platform investments, creators and communities, social search and AI visibility, and social media's impact on business objectives. According to the report findings, 87% of marketers say AI has improved their team's productivity, yet fewer than half (48%) say their team can confidently demonstrate social media ROI to leadership with clear attribution and data.

The report also highlights findings on team capacity and burnout among marketing organizations, with more than half of respondents saying they use AI tools their company has not approved at least some of the time—up from 42% last year.

"In 2027, the strongest social strategies will not be defined by how much content teams can produce. They will be defined by how well they turn every interaction into measurable business value and a better customer experience," said Claire Wilson, CMO, Emplifi.

Key insights from the report:

  • AI and productivity: Only 38% of marketers report a significant productivity increase from AI, so for most teams the gains are meaningful rather than transformational. Adoption is strongest in caption and copywriting (72%), ideation (70%), image generation (64%) and reporting and analytics (64%), while 60% are not yet using AI for community management.
  • AI governance: 37% of organizations have a fully defined AI policy for marketing and a further 41% have partial guidelines. Brand safety and content quality is the biggest barrier to broader AI adoption (26%), ahead of lack of skills or training (19%) and integration with existing tools (16%).
  • Proving impact: Reach and impressions (58%) and engagement rate are the KPIs marketers most often rank in their top three, while fewer than one in three rank social-attributed revenue among their top three KPIs. Attribution is the most commonly cited reporting obstacle.
  • Reporting time: 62% of marketers spend four or more hours a week on reporting and analytics. Over the past 12 months, 69% say AI has saved their team three or more hours a week on it.
  • Social search and AI visibility: 86% say optimizing social content for discovery and search is a formal priority or on their radar for the next 12 months, and 48% actively monitor how their brand appears in tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity. Three in four have adapted social content to improve visibility in AI-generated results, but only just over a third work from a defined strategy. For around one in five organizations, nobody owns AI visibility or no defined approach exists.
  • Influencers and platforms: 53% of marketers expect their influencer budget to increase over the next 12 months. Among teams that have a budget, 64% plan to increase it, in line with last year (67%). Plans to increase collaborations with virtual or AI-generated influencers have fallen to 35% from 58%. Instagram is the top platform for planned investment, and Reddit is the only platform where the share planning to increase investment (31%) exceeds the share currently using it for marketing (28%).
  • Team capacity and burnout: 54% say their social team has grown in the past year, and 86% say content and campaign volume has increased. Four in five describe their workload as manageable, in line with last year, but the share who feel burnout very often has risen to 24% from 17%. Marketers name smarter automation (21%) and better AI tools (18%) together about twice as often as additional headcount (20%) as the change that would most improve team capacity and output.

Looking ahead, AI tools and automation are marketers' top investment priority for the next 12 months (31%), ahead of short-form video production (19%) and analytics and reporting (15%). Three in four expect AI's role on their team to grow over the next two years.

"AI is giving social teams hours back, with more than two in three saving three or more a week on reporting. The question now is how that time is used. Teams that pour it into more content will only add to the pressure. Teams that invest it in listening, responding, and better judgment will deliver stronger customer experiences and work their people can sustain." Wilson added.

To download the complete report, visit: The State of Social Media Marketing 2027 from Emplifi.

Emplifi will discuss the findings in a live webinar with creator and social strategist Lia Haberman on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 11 a.m. ET. To register for "Unpacking the State of Social Media Marketing 2027 with Lia Haberman," visit the registration page.

Survey Methodology: Emplifi partnered with Alchemer to conduct an online survey of 405 marketing managers, directors and executives in the US, UK, Australia, and New Zealand in September 2026. Respondents work full-time in marketing-related roles at companies with 11+ employees, have 3+ years in their industry and influence marketing technology purchases. Comparisons with The State of Social Media Marketing 2026 (n=564) are directional, as the samples differ in geography, company size and qualification criteria, and some question wording differs.

About Emplifi

Emplifi is the only Autonomous CX platform unifying social marketing, commerce, and customer care for more than 22,000 brands worldwide. Powered by Fuel AI, built on more than 5T of data, and recognized as a leader by leading industry analysts, Emplifi helps enterprise teams orchestrate connected customer journeys and deliver personalized experiences at scale, turning every customer touchpoint into a competitive advantage.

releases.body:
NEW YORK, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Better Business Advice has named CapCut a top choice in a 2026 review of AI software for social media marketing, highlighting support for campaign planning, advertising concepts, and post-launch creative revisions. The review examines how businesses can use AI-assisted tools to develop promotional materials around marketing objectives rather than simply produce more social media content.

The recognition addresses a practical challenge for small businesses and lean marketing teams. A single promotion may require multiple advertising angles, visual formats, approvals, and adjustments after launch. CapCut supports several stages of that process through three creative tools.

Best AI Software for Social Media Marketing:

  • Seedream - CapCut's AI image generator that turns written marketing briefs into visual concepts, mood boards, and promotional image drafts.
  • Seedance 2.0 - CapCut's AI video generator that creates motion-based drafts for advertising hooks, product demonstrations, launch teasers, and campaign storyboards.
  • AI Image Extender - CapCut's image editing tool that expands backgrounds to help adapt campaign visuals for different layouts and advertising placements.

Why CapCut Is a Practical Choice for Social Media Marketing

Social media campaigns begin with a business objective, whether generating leads, increasing store visits, or driving online sales. Effective creative assets need to communicate a relevant benefit, present a clear offer, and support the intended action.

Better Business Advice recognizes CapCut for helping translate those priorities into visual materials. Seedream supports early direction, Seedance 2.0 supports promotional video concepts, and AI Image Extender supports subsequent adaptations. The combined workflow is particularly relevant when production resources are limited, or campaigns require frequent updates.

The advantage is flexibility across campaign stages, not automatic marketing decisions. Businesses still determine audience targeting, offers, budgets, and performance goals.

How Seedream Helps Turn Marketing Briefs Into Visual Campaign Concepts

A product can support several promotional messages. A travel mug, for example, might be positioned around everyday commuting, outdoor activities, or temperature retention. Each approach calls for a different visual treatment.

Seedream converts prompts into concept images that can be compared before a photo shoot or final design is commissioned. Better Business Advice identifies three elements that make those prompts more useful:

  • Audience and objective: Define the customer and desired response.
  • Offer and message: Specify the benefit, promotion, or customer problem.
  • Creative direction: Establish setting, tone, branding requirements, and format.

This structure helps reviewers judge visual drafts against the campaign brief rather than personal preference alone. Generated imagery still requires checks for product accuracy, brand consistency, and realistic advertising claims before publication.

How Seedance 2.0 Supports Testing Different Social Media Ad Messages

Video advertising often depends on the opening message. A demonstration highlighting a product feature may appeal to a different audience than a lifestyle-led promotion of the same item.

Seedance 2.0 can turn alternative written concepts into motion drafts for storyboards, launch teasers, and product demonstrations. That capability makes exploring distinct advertising hooks more practical before committing to full production.

The Better Business Advice review also connects creative variations with A/B testing. A controlled comparison might change the opening scene while keeping the audience, offer, and landing page consistent. Marketers can then assess whether the creative difference affects the intended result.

CapCut creates visual materials; advertising platforms supply performance data. Relevant measures include click-through rate for traffic campaigns, qualified leads for inquiry campaigns, and cost per purchase for online sales. High view counts alone do not establish advertising effectiveness.

How AI Image Extender Helps Refine Campaign Assets After Launch

Campaign results frequently call for targeted changes rather than complete redesigns. A successful product visual might need a wider format, while a closely cropped image might require extra room for a headline.

AI Image Extender generates space around an existing image, helping adjust composition for another advertising placement while retaining the main subject. The revised asset still needs inspection for visual accuracy and commercial-use requirements.

Better Business Advice outlines a performance-informed revision cycle: review the objective, identify the weak point, change a relevant element, and compare the new version. Low click-through rates may suggest a clearer hook. Strong clicks but weak sales could instead indicate an issue with pricing or the landing page.

The distinction prevents unnecessary creative changes and keeps revisions linked to the campaign's actual goal.

What Better Business Advice's Recognition Means for Marketing Teams

Better Business Advice identifies CapCut as a top choice because the platform supports three connected needs: campaign concept development, promotional message exploration, and practical visual adaptation. These capabilities can help small businesses and ecommerce teams manage recurring promotions without treating every creative variation as a separate production project.

The full review can be read at the Better Business Advice website.

About CapCut

CapCut is an AI-powered photo and video editing platform designed to make high-quality video creation accessible across devices. The platform supports creators, businesses, and everyday users with tools for video editing, AI video generation, captions, templates, audio, and visual editing. CapCut is available across mobile, web, desktop, and iPad experiences, helping users create, edit, and prepare video content for social media, marketing, education, and personal projects.

Employers reach qualified frontline candidates where they already spend their time, and candidates go from a social post to a phone interview in minutes.

NEW YORK, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Classet, the AI phone screener for high-volume hiring, and Reelist, the automated social sourcing platform, today announced a partnership that connects employers with frontline candidates on social media and interviews them within minutes of applying. Together, the two companies give employers a reliable source of qualified, interviewed applicants. Through the integration, customers can source candidates from Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok with one click via Reelist, directly from the Classet platform. Candidates apply in a few taps without ever leaving the app they're scrolling, and Joy, Classet's AI recruiter, calls them within minutes for a structured phone interview.

Candidates go from a social post to an AI phone interview in minutes, with no job board in between.

For employers: Eliminate wasteful job-board spend and hours chasing candidates for interviews.

Teams hiring frontline, skilled trades, and healthcare workers spend most of their recruiting budget on job boards, often with little to show for it. The best workers are usually already employed and not searching job boards, but more than 80% of working adults spend time on social media every day. With Reelist and Classet, employers meet those candidates where they are and have them screened before a recruiter spends a minute on them. Recruiters start the day with candidates who meet their must-have criteria and are ready to schedule.

Reelist customers see up to 3x higher retention and 30% lower cost per hire from social applicants compared with job-board applicants.

And with Classet, employers saw 12% more offers, 18% more starts, and 17% higher retention because Joy surfaces qualified candidates to recruiting teams within minutes.

For candidates: from social post to interview in minutes

Candidates see a job in the feed they already scroll and apply without leaving the app. Instead of waiting days for a callback, they get a phone interview within minutes, day or night, and can ask their own questions about pay, schedule, and the role. They know quickly whether the job is a good fit, and so does the employer. Candidates like it: in Classet's study of 10,167 post-interview ratings, 88% rated their AI phone interview positively.

How it works

  1. Launch from Classet. A recruiter selects the jobs to fill, and with one click, Reelist starts sourcing candidates on social media automatically.
  2. Apply on social media. Candidates see the employer's job in their TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook feed and apply in a few taps.
  3. Interviewed within minutes. Joy calls applicants as soon as they apply, runs the employer's custom phone interview in 25+ languages, answers questions, and flags who meets the must-have criteria. A human makes every hiring decision.
  4. One pipeline. Qualified applicants flow into Classet or into the customer's ATS, with a summary, transcript, and recording for each interview.

From Classet

"Our customers are tired of paying job boards for applicants who never hear back," said Nick Jones, COO and Co-Founder of Classet. "Reelist reaches great candidates where they already are, and Joy interviews them immediately, day or night. Candidates find out fast whether the job is right for them, and recruiters start their morning with people who are qualified and ready to work."

From Reelist

"For years, job boards were the only option for frontline hiring. Not anymore," said Katy Schuck, COO of Reelist. "Employers can recruit qualified workers on social media as easily as posting a job, get every applicant interviewed within minutes, and finally take control of their own hiring."

Availability

The Reelist integration is available now to Classet customers in the platform.

About Reelist

Reelist is the automated social sourcing platform for frontline hiring, from nurses and skilled trades to restaurant general managers. Instead of relying on job board traffic, Reelist puts employers' open roles in front of local candidates on Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok, where they already spend their time. Candidates apply in a few taps, and qualified applicants flow directly into the employer's applicant tracking system, ready for a recruiter to call. Reelist integrates with more than 65 applicant tracking systems and has reached over 10 million job seekers on social media. The company is headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia. Learn more at reelist.com.

About Classet

Classet is the AI recruiting solution for teams hiring hourly, skilled-trades, and frontline workers. Joy, Classet's AI recruiter, calls applicants within moments of applying, day or night, runs a structured phone interview in 25+ languages, and delivers a summary, transcript, and recording for every candidate. Classet Hiring Hub then handles the repetitive work of an ATS, including stage moves, follow-ups, and scheduling, on its own. Joy has interviewed hundreds of thousands of applicants for 500+ hiring teams and connects to 100+ applicant tracking systems. Founded by the team that hired more than one million W2 hourly workers at Bluecrew, Classet is headquartered in Chicago. Learn more at classet.ai.

("Kidoodle", and together with APMC, the "Debtors"), is soliciting offers to purchase or invest in the Debtors' business and assets, including the Kidoodle.TV and Victory+ streaming platforms, pursuant to a Court-approved stalking horse sale and investment solicitation process (the "SISP").

  • Victory+ is a free, ad-supported live sports streaming service launched in 2024; the platform is currently offline.

  • Proprietary programmatic advertising stack and COPPA-compliant advertising proxy.
  • Data lake and first-party user data (subject to applicable privacy law), content and media rights contracts, computer equipment and accounts receivable.

releases.body:
45% of pay-TV subscribers use pay TV to access live video, while 25% of US internet households use FAST services

PLANO, Texas, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Parks Associates' research The New Live TV Model: Skinny Bundles, Sports, News finds 39% of US internet households watch live events or sports through an on-demand streaming service, showing the growing role of streaming services in delivering live programming. The expanding mix of options to watch video is changing how consumers find and watch sports, news, and events, as live video viewing is no longer synonymous with pay TV.

Parks Associates research also finds:

  • 25% watch live video through free ad-supported television (FAST) services.
  • 21% report they don't watch live video at all.

"Consumers value live content but struggle to find and access it," said Michael Goodman, Director, Entertainment Research, Parks Associates. "The challenge for providers is making live content accessible. Sports is a good example, with programming now distributed across multiple services and platforms."

Consumer interest in live sports is growing alongside broad-appeal entertainment. According to Parks Associates consumer research, comedy (60%), drama (56%), and news (50%) are the most popular content categories, while 48% report watching live sports. Subscription VOD (SVOD) services continue to add sports, news, and live events while FAST services build engagement through curated linear channels.

"Competition for viewers is increasingly about more than the content itself," Goodman said. "Providers need to deliver an experience that makes it easy for consumers to find, access, and move between live and on-demand programming."

  • OnVibe has launched a new agentic AI system that streamlines content creation and helps businesses get greater value and build social media presence more effectively.
  • New features include in-depth performance evaluations for Instagram and LinkedIn that identify what's working,  where content falls short and opportunities for improvement, at no cost.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OnVibe, an AI-powered social marketing company backed by LG NOVA, LG Electronics' North America Innovation Center, today unveiled a new agentic AI system that powers its social marketing platform, carrying business context from content recommendations through creation and Instagram publishing.

AI has made it easy to generate a post in seconds. As feeds fill with content that looks and sounds alike, the harder work is knowing which ideas reflect a business, connect with its audience and deserve a place in the feed. For founders and small teams, that work competes with building products, serving customers and running day-to-day operations.

The system brings together ideas, writing, visual creation, scheduling and Instagram publishing in one conversation, helping businesses turn ideas into finished posts with fewer steps. It delivers daily content ideas shaped by each business's context and helps users develop their chosen ideas into finished posts. Users can also ask it to develop a content plan and schedule posts across multiple days.

"Small teams have enough to do without figuring out what to ask an AI each morning," said OnVibe CEO Sahar Arshad. "OnVibe looks at what has worked for your business, what your audience responds to and what is happening in your niche. It brings you ideas with a reason behind each one. You choose the direction, and the same conversation can take it all the way to publication."

Acting as a personal AI agent for the business's Instagram, OnVibe has an informed memory and adapts to the client's work style to provide professional, customized guidance aligned with the business's needs and goals, so businesses can confidently decide what to post.

OnVibe's VibeCheck helps businesses and creators understand what's working in their social content, where the gaps are and what to post next. It evaluates positioning, content pillars and engagement patterns, then provides suggested posts and practical recommendations to strengthen their social presence. For accounts with existing content, OnVibe can analyze up to 50 recent posts to understand content patterns and audience response. The feature helps users assess posting consistency, engagement and content formats.

Free evaluations are available at audit.onvibe.co, with no platform signup required, for Instagram business and creator accounts, as well as LinkedIn profiles of founders and executives and LinkedIn company pages.

How the New System Works

OnVibe's agentic system is designed to carry context and work across the steps involved in social marketing:

  • Ideas that arrive ready to develop: Daily Drop offers content ideas tailored to the business, with creative direction, suggested copy or scripts, captions, hashtags and visuals. Each idea includes an explanation of why it was recommended.
  • Memory users can shape: OnVibe builds on what it learns about a business's voice, visual style, goals, location, market and preferences across conversations. Users can review and update that memory, upload their own images and add PDF brand guidelines. They can also ask why a particular idea fits.
  • A conversation that adapts to the task: Users can request a precise edit or provide a broader brief. They can refine a static post, build a carousel or generate a multi-day content plan, then schedule or publish finished posts directly to Instagram within the same conversation.
  • Writing guided by practitioners: Captions follow guidance developed by OnVibe's social media experts to help the writing sound specific to the business.

The free Starter Plan supports one connected Instagram account and requires no credit card. Higher creation limits are currently available at no cost for a limited time.

Expert Support Through OnVibe Concierge

OnVibe's Concierge program provides businesses with a team to manage their social presence using OnVibe's Agentic AI Engine. Its strategists and creatives handle social strategy, content creation, publishing and performance across Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok and Facebook, using OnVibe's AI engine as the backend to refine the work over time. In two months, OnVibe Concierge helped an early-stage technology client triple its follower count while increasing posting frequency from one to five posts per week across four social channels. To build awareness and make the product's value more relatable, OnVibe developed a consistent brand voice, content built around real-world experiences, user-generated content and a paid distribution strategy.

Concierge supports ongoing social marketing as well as company launches, product introductions and entry into new markets, including international businesses launching in the U.S. The team helps sharpen the message and carry the story across the channels where the business needs to build an audience.

Why It Matters Now

Social media is an important way for businesses to be discovered, yet maintaining a presence often falls to people wearing many hats. According to Constant Contact's Q2 2026 Small Business Now report, 49 percent of consumers surveyed globally use social media to find new small businesses, compared with 40 percent who use search engines. The report also found that 47 percent of small business owners surveyed manage their social media entirely on their own.

To get started with OnVibe, visit onvibe.co. To request a free Instagram or LinkedIn performance evaluation, visit audit.onvibe.co.

SAN DIEGO, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sony Electronics Inc. today announced new premium Walkman® digital media players – NW-WM1ZM3, NW-WM1AM3, and NW-ZX900. Designed for music enthusiasts and audiophiles, the new Walkman models are engineered to deliver exceptional sound and incorporate a wealth of premium audio components throughout their design.

The NW-WM1ZM3 and NW-WM1AM3 bring together Sony's most advanced audio technologies, including key components made from oxygen-free copper, for uncompromising sound quality. The WM1 Series is designed to convey the artist's original intent, delivering detailed, high-resolution sound. Developed in pursuit of exceptional sound quality, it captures subtle nuances throughout a performance, while maintaining clarity, scale, and dynamics at higher volumes.

The NW-ZX900 inherits many of the same premium audio components used in Sony's flagship model, the NW-WMZM3, delivering exceptional sound quality with a sleek design.

Class-leading components deliver the highest possible sonic performance

The NW-WM1ZM3 is built around a precision-machined, gold-plated oxygen-free copper (OFC) chassis, engineered specifically to further elevate the sound quality of this flagship model. It features a 99.99% (4N) purity OFC main chassis and an OFC rear chassis. These are secured with screws featuring a low-resistance gold-plated treatment applied exclusively for this model, providing a stable ground connection that delivers powerful bass, an expansive soundstage, and smooth, extended high frequencies. Thick KIMBER KABLE® wiring, inherited from Sony's DMP-Z1, further reduces noise and preserves signal integrity for rich, detailed sound.

The NW-WM1AM3 and NW-ZX900 adopt a similar design philosophy, combining an aluminium-alloy main chassis with a gold-plated OFC rear chassis to enhance rigidity and sound quality.

The NW-WM1ZM3 and NW-WM1AM3 further evolve Sony's premium power circuitry with a significant enhancement to the power supply architecture: the previous single large solid high-polymer capacitor has been replaced by dual large solid high-polymer capacitors. Together with hand-soldered OFC wiring, this advanced configuration helps provide cleaner, more stable power with minimal interference.

A larger, high-purity 4N copper coil is used in the L-C filter to optimize the balanced output signal from the digital amplifier. Its flat conductive wire reduces resistance and distortion, enhancing clarity and detail across the frequency range. An OFC milled block covering the digital section also strengthens the digital ground. With approximately 34% greater mass than the previous model, it helps further reduce noise and reproduce sound with greater clarity and definition.

The NW-ZX900 also benefits from new premium parts, including an ultra-low noise LDO regulator and crystal oscillators that are the same as those used in the higher-end models.

Unique sound processing technology gives you more ways to enjoy different types of music

The S-Master™ HX digital amp technology, independently developed for Walkman, helps deliver powerful, detailed sound. It is compatible with support for Native DSD format and supports balanced and high-power output. It now also includes a look-ahead noise shaper that predicts quantization noise in advance and applies optimal processing, providing excellent responsiveness to fast transients and delivering clearer, faster sound reproduction.

 All three players run Sony's DSD Remastering Engine, which resamples PCM audio into an 11.2MHz DSD ultra-high-frequency stream for a character closer to analogue. The new range has been updated so listeners can enjoy DSD Remastering Engine whether music is streamed over Wi-Fi® or downloaded.

Long battery life

The NW-WM1ZM3 and NW-WM1AM3 deliver up to 35 hours[1] of 128kbps MP3 playback and an improved streaming battery life of up to 31 hours[2]. The NW-ZX900 has a battery life of up to 40 hours1 of 128kbps MP3 playback, or up to 35 hours2 with the streaming service apps[3] to meet user's demand.

The NW-WM1ZM3 and NW-WM1AM3 feature a larger 5.5" screen, while the NW-ZX900 is available with a 5" screen. These large screens are smooth and responsive, improving operability, and the Walkman® Home Screen interface can be customised to suit your needs. The album cover, an integral part of the listening experience, is now larger and clearer.

Sustainability in mind

These new models are not only designed to be stylish but also with the environment in mind. No plastic is used in the packaging material for the NW-WM1ZM3, NW-WM1AM3 and NW-ZX900[4], reflecting Sony's commitment to reducing the environmental impact of our products and practices.

  • The NW-ZX900 is available for pre-order from Sony, Crutchfield, B&H, and Amazon now with a suggested retail price of $1,899.99 US / $2,659.99 CAN. Additional authorized dealers' availability will follow.

California Lutheran University Center for Nonprofit Leadership workshop will provide nonprofit leaders with practical strategies to strengthen engagement, fundraising and mission-driven social media

THOUSAND OAKS, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marketing Maven CEO and president Lindsey Carnett will lead "Strategic Social Media for Nonprofit Growth and Engagement," a three-hour virtual workshop presented by California Lutheran University's Center for Nonprofit Leadership with support from the Santa Barbara Foundation on Wednesday, November 4, 2026 from 9 a.m. to noon.

Designed for nonprofit leaders, communications and marketing staff and board members, the workshop will provide practical strategies for using social media to build awareness, engage supporters and advance organizational missions. Participants will explore how different social media platforms can support organizational objectives, including volunteer recruitment, donor cultivation, event promotion, corporate partnerships and talent acquisition.

"Social media gives nonprofits an incredible opportunity to connect directly with the communities they serve, but being active online is only one piece of an effective strategy," said Carnett. "This workshop is designed to give nonprofit leaders practical tools they can use to create meaningful content, strengthen engagement and turn their social media efforts into measurable support for their missions."

Throughout the workshop, Carnett will guide participants through developing a social media strategy aligned with their organizational priorities and identifying the platforms best suited to reach their audiences. Attendees will learn strategies for creating compelling content, developing an efficient content calendar and using scheduling and analytics tools to maximize their time and impact. The workshop will also address organic and paid social media, current platform trends and ways to integrate social media into broader fundraising and marketing campaigns.

Support from the Santa Barbara Foundation provides nonprofit professionals serving Santa Barbara County access to professional development opportunities through Cal Lutheran's Center for Nonprofit Leadership. The Nov. 4 workshop is part of the Foundation's support for nonprofit learning and development in the region.

Carnett brings more than two decades of marketing and public relations experience to the workshop. As founder and CEO of Marketing Maven, an integrated marketing and public relations agency, her areas of expertise include public relations, social media, reputation management, search engine optimization and digital advertising. A Cal Lutheran alumna, Carnett also serves as a faculty lecturer for the university's Center for Nonprofit Leadership and earned her bachelor's degree in Spanish and communications with an emphasis in public relations and advertising.

The workshop will be held virtually via Zoom on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, from 9 a.m. to noon. releases.body:
Transition to Inox Solar Americas digital platforms will maintain continuity for Boviet Solar customers, technical support and warranty inquiries

GREENVILLE, N.C., Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Inox Solar Americas LLC, a U.S.-based solar technology and manufacturing company specializing in the production of advanced PV cells and high-performance PV modules for the U.S. solar market, today announced that the Boviet Solar website, social media platforms, and other external brand touchpoints will begin a gradual transition to the Inox Solar Americas brand as part of the ongoing integration of Boviet Solar's U.S. business and operations into Inox Solar Americas.

Earlier this year, Inox Solar Americas acquired Boviet Solar's U.S. PV module manufacturing and PV cell manufacturing assets in Greenville, North Carolina, as well as its U.S. commercial operations. The acquisition established the foundation for Inox Solar Americas' growing U.S. solar manufacturing and commercial platform.

GRADUAL BRAND TRANSITION

The brand transition will be implemented in phases across website content, social media channels, company and product information, marketing communications, trade shows, industry events, customer-facing materials, and other external brand touchpoints, progressively transitioning from Boviet Solar to the Inox Solar Americas brand.

During the transition period, customers, partners, and other industry stakeholders may continue to see both the Boviet Solar and Inox Solar Americas names across certain websites, social media platforms, product materials, technical documentation, trade shows, industry events, and other communications.

The transition will be managed progressively to maintain continuity and access to important product, technical, and customer information while establishing Inox Solar Americas as the company's U.S. solar manufacturing and commercial brand.

The transition represents another important step in the integration of Boviet Solar's U.S. business into Inox Solar Americas and the continued development and expansion of the company's U.S. solar manufacturing platform.

Additional updates regarding the Boviet Solar brand transition and related platforms, materials, and communications will be provided as the integration progresses.

CONTINUED SUPPORT FOR BOVIET SOLAR CUSTOMERS

Existing Boviet Solar customers and partners requiring customer service, PV module technical support, warranty assistance, product information or other product-related support can continue to submit inquiries through inoxsolar.us/company/contact-us. Inquiries submitted through the website will be directed to Boviet Solar's Global team for review and follow-up.

INOX SOLAR AMERICAS

Inox Solar Americas, founded in 2026 in the United States, is a leading solar technology and manufacturing company specializing in advanced monocrystalline PV cells and high-performance Gamma Series™ monofacial and Vega Series™ bifacial PV modules. Inox Solar Americas' photovoltaic solutions are engineered to meet the needs of residential, commercial, industrial, community solar, and utility-scale applications, delivering exceptional efficiency, reliability, and long-term value.

Inox Solar Americas acquired Boviet Solar's U.S. PV manufacturing assets in Greenville, North Carolina, USA, including 3.0 GW of annual PV module manufacturing capacity and 3.0 GW of planned annual PV cell manufacturing capacity, expected to come online in 2027. Through localized manufacturing, resilient supply chains, operational excellence, and efficient logistics, Inox Solar Americas is helping strengthen the U.S. solar supply chain and meet growing domestic demand.

Inox Solar Americas is part of the broader renewable energy platform of Inox Clean Energy and the INOXGFL Group, headquartered in India. Backed by the group's financial strength, business stability, manufacturing capabilities, technological innovation, and industry expertise, Inox Solar Americas is committed to delivering high-quality, reliable, and sustainable solar solutions to customers across the U.S. solar energy market.

For more information, visit: inoxsolar.us, inoxclean.com and inoxgfl.com.

releases.title: From Courtroom to TikTok: New Alcatraz East Exhibit Explores How Social Media Is Changing Crime Coverage
releases.body:
The Alcatraz East Crime Museum is opening a new exhibit showcasing pop culture crime influencer Stephanie Giancristofaro

PIGEON FORGE, Tenn., Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alcatraz East Crime Museum is opening a new exhibit showcasing TikTok's influence on modern crime reporting. The exhibit will feature Stephanie Giancristofaro, a criminal defense attorney who has become an influencer on TikTok with over 326,000 followers. This exhibit comes on the 10th anniversary of the popular app being used by an audience of all ages.

"There is a tremendous amount of information, and misinformation, surrounding high-profile criminal cases online," said Giancristofaro. "I use my platform to bring the conversation back to the facts: what the evidence actually shows, what the law actually says, and what is simply speculation. People are entitled to their own opinions, but those opinions should start with accurate information."

Giancristofaro started posting videos on TikTok after seeing that the public often struggles to understand the legalities involved in criminal cases. After the murder of four college students at the University of Idaho in 2022, she began making videos to help people gain a better understanding of the criminal defense process and laws regarding the case. People appreciated the videos because Giancristofaro helped clarify confusing information about the case they were seeing dominate the headlines.  This led her to continue with other cases so people could better understand the issues in terms they could easily grasp.

According to the Pew Research Center, 37% of adults in the U.S. report that they use TikTok, and that number continues to grow each year. They report that around 55% of adults who use the popular app regularly get their news from it, while 95% say they use it for entertainment purposes. Giancristofaro's videos get millions of views, showing how much interest people have in that type of content.

On September 20, 2026, TikTok celebrates its 10th anniversary. Originally launched as Douyin from a small apartment in China in 2016, it expanded internationally a year later. The popularity of the app was greatly boosted in 2018, when it merged with the app Musical.ly, which featured people lip-syncing to songs. TikTok has surged in popularity as people find that the algorithm excels in serving up content that is unique to each person's interest. It has become an outlet for influencers of all types to find their unique audience, including for those who are interested in crime news, criminal defense, and related issues.

"The new TikTok influencer exhibit is going to be a fascinating  addition to our pop culture section," said Ally Mills, artifacts and programs manager at Alcatraz East Crime Museum. "It's become a widely used platform and continues to grow in popularity. People are now using it to get information about criminal cases and more."

The museum features over 100 exhibits and interactives, as well as four temporary exhibit spaces, showcasing many famous items, including Al Capone's rosary, Ted Bundy's dental molds, and Charles Manson's acoustic guitar. This top museum is open daily at 10 am. The last tickets are sold 60 minutes before closing. These interactive experiences are available for an additional fee for birthday parties, school groups, scouts, team building, or other special events. To get a discounted rate for groups of 15 or more, complete the online form and allow up to 72 hours for confirmation. For more information about tickets, discounts, temporary exhibits, and all the museum has to offer, visit the website: https://www.alcatrazeast.com.

Alcatraz East Crime Museum has updated its board of crime experts, which includes Derwin Bradley, a retired master police officer; James R. Knight, a crime writer; Robin Maynard, a certified crime scene investigator in Florida; Derek Newport, a law enforcement veteran who worked for the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation for 20 years; and Judge Belvin Perry, Jr., who presided over the notorious case against Casey Anthony, among others.

About Alcatraz East

Alcatraz East is the most arresting crime museum in the United States. Guests of all ages can embark on a unique journey through the history of American crime, crime-solving, and the justice system. Through interactive exhibits and original artifacts, Alcatraz East is an entertaining and educational experience for all ages - so much fun it's a crime! This family attraction is at The Island's entrance, 2757 Parkway, Pigeon Forge, TN. The last ticket is sold 60 minutes before closing. For more information and to purchase tickets, visit www.alcatrazeast.com.

releases.body:
RM11 identifies the rise of owned audiences, diversified monetization, paid traffic, AI automation and creator wellness as forces reshaping the creator business model.

DALLAS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The creator economy is growing up. Building a large following is no longer enough to build a sustainable creator business as creators increasingly seek greater control over their audiences, revenue, workload and long-term careers.

RM11, a creator-first platform built around direct audience relationships and multiple monetization tools, has identified five trends it believes will reshape how creators build businesses and generate revenue in 2027.

Recent industry research supports that shift. CreatorIQ's 2026 State of Creators study, based on 5,095 creators, found that 67% earned less than $10,000 from content creation over the prior year and that content creation was not the primary source of income for 62% of respondents. Meanwhile, Epidemic Sound's Future of the Creator Economy Report 2026 found that 72% of creators are actively developing owned audiences, while 41% want to build a sustainable independent business or grow into a media brand or creator studio.

"The next evolution of the creator economy isn't about producing more content or accumulating more followers," said Olivier David, Chief Growth Officer of RM11. "It's about giving creators the infrastructure to operate like businesses — own their audience relationships, diversify revenue, acquire customers and protect their most valuable resource: their time."

RM11 identifies five shifts that will define the next era of creator monetization:

1. Owned audiences will become more valuable than follower counts.

Creators are increasingly looking beyond algorithm-dependent reach toward direct relationships with their audiences. Memberships, private communities, messaging and direct-to-fan experiences can give creators greater control over how they engage and monetize their most loyal followers. Epidemic Sound's 2026 research found 72% of creators are already developing audiences away from core platforms through channels such as newsletters and Discord.

2. Creator platforms will evolve beyond the paywall.

The next generation of creator platforms will function more like business operating systems. Rather than relying on subscriptions alone, creators will increasingly combine memberships, pay-per-view content, livestreams, messaging, video calls and other revenue streams while using integrated tools to manage customer relationships, content and day-to-day operations.

3. Creators will start thinking about customer acquisition — not just followers.

As the industry matures, creators will increasingly apply traditional business metrics such as customer acquisition cost, conversion and return on advertising spend to audience growth. RM11 is developing promotion tools designed to make paid traffic and measurable customer acquisition more accessible to eligible creators, moving growth beyond the traditional "post and hope" model.

4. AI will shift from content generation to workload reduction.

AI adoption is becoming mainstream, but creator control remains critical. Adobe's 2026 Creators' Toolkit Report found that 93% of surveyed creators say creative AI helps them produce content faster, while 85% say the final creative decision should always remain with the creator. RM11 believes the next opportunity lies in using AI to reduce repetitive work and expand creator capacity without sacrificing authenticity, ownership or human oversight.

5. Creator wellness will become business infrastructure.

Creator-first economics cannot stop at revenue share. As creators operate increasingly complex businesses, platforms will be expected to help address the workload, stress and burnout that can accompany always-on digital careers. RM11 is investing in this area through integrated human account-management support and relationships with creator wellness and mental health organizations, including Creators for Mental Health, Revive Health Therapy and Pineapple Support.

"At RM11, 'creator-first' has to mean more than a revenue split," David added. "It means asking what creators actually need to build sustainable businesses — and then building the technology, services and partnerships around them."

RM11's growing ecosystem combines direct monetization, creator CRM capabilities, human account-management support, audience-growth initiatives and creator wellness resources as the company works toward a broader vision: giving creators the infrastructure to build businesses, not simply profiles.

Through memberships, exclusive content, messaging, livestreaming, native video calls, integrated creator tools, account-management support, and a free CRM for agencies, RM11 provides multiple ways for creators to monetize direct relationships with their audiences. Female-founded and led, RM11 is building a more sustainable, creator-first model for the next generation of the creator economy.
